newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico expels another human-rights worker.
newsitem.headline: Mexico expels another human-rights worker.

text.p: George Ann Potter, the international programmes director for the Unitarian Universalist Service Committee, was expelled by Mexican authorities this week, the committee said on Friday.
Potter was the third human-rights worker expelled this week, the Cambridge, Massachusetts, church group said.
On Sunday, two Central American human-rights workers were forced to leave Mexico. Like Potter, they were given 72 hours to leave the country for using the wrong type of visa.

"While Potter was told that the official reason for her explusion centred around her use of the wrong type of visa, the service committee believes that this is part of an emerging pattern of expulsions of international human-rights workers by the Mexican government," the service committee said.
A spokeswoman at the Mexican Interior Ministry, which regulates immigration matters, said the ministry had no information on the case and could not comment.
The two Central Americans, Vilma Nunez of Nicaragua and Benjamin Cuellar of El Salvador, were affiliated with the Paris-based Federation of Human Rights Leagues (FIDH).
The FIDH also said the expulsions came "in the context of growing repression against defenders of Mexican human rights."
Potter was in Mexico to attend the Latin American Scholars Association Conference and to visit local human rights groups in the troubled southern state of Oaxaca.
The Central Americans were working in the neighbouring state of Guerrero. Both states are populated largely by poor peasants and have been home to guerrilla activity in recent months.

"The Mexican government is aware that the UUSC has monitored and documented the harassment of its partner groups and other human-rights workers by the government and military," the service committee said. "UUSC has reported these incidents to the Mexican and U.S. governments."
The service committee said in the statement that it "advances human rights" in the United States, Latin America, Africa and Asia through local partner groups.
